import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # Columns expected in target schema
    target_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']

    # Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and correct types
        df = df[target_columns].copy()
        df['admit'] = df['admit'].astype(int)
        df['gre'] = df['gre'].astype(int)
        df['gpa'] = df['gpa'].astype(float)
        df['prestige'] = df['prestige'].astype(int)
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union all)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Since all sources have the same schema and represent similar data,
    # the transformation is a union of all source tables.
    # No additional aggregation or join is needed based on the problem statement.

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_84/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
